title: Impact of training intensity distribution on performance in endurance athletes
authors: Esteve-Lanao J, Foster C, Seiler S, Lucia A
journal: Journal of Strength and Conditioning Research
population: Sub-elite endurance runners (mostly 5000 m track specialists who also race 9-12 km cross-country)
findings: 12 runners randomised to low-intensity (Z1) or between-thresholds (Z2) emphasis; HR-controlled for 5 months.
Improvement in a simulated 10.4 km cross-country race was greater in Z1 (-157+/-13 s) than Z2 (-121.5+/-7.1 s), p = 0.03.
Authors conclude the results support a relatively large share of low-intensity training over about 5 months, provided high-intensity training remains sufficient.
limitations: Only 12 runners; zone 3 dose was matched in both arms, so the trial tests displacement of moderate-intensity time and not polarized vs pyramidal. Single race outcome. Evidence level lowered from B to C because of sample size.
implications: Replacing zone 2 (between-threshold) time with zone 1 while holding about 8% in zone 3 is a defensible default for sub-elite runners over multi-month blocks.
Do not drop zone 3 below about 8% of time on this evidence alone.
Zone 2 share of about 12% (versus about 25%) is the contrast supported here; treat about 12% as a base-phase ceiling, not a validated optimum.

verification.notes: Crossref matches title, JSCR, 2007. All numbers confirmed in Europe PMC abstract. Evidence level downgraded B to C (n=12).
